package.description: Use when a dispatch poll supplies closed and open counts, or when counts must be derived from a ticket log.
package.instructions:
Identify which case the input matches before replying. The two cases have different input requirements and different output formats; do not mix them or emit both formats for one input.

CASE 1 - COUNTS SUPPLIED
Input requirement: the request explicitly supplies closed and open counts.
Output: one line using the exact pattern CURATOR-POLL | closed <closed count> of <total count> | pending <open count>.
Derive the total as closed plus open.
See references/daily-format.md for the worked example.

CASE 2 - TICKET LOG
Input requirement: a log of ticket IDs and statuses, with counts not supplied.
Processing: deduplicate by ticket ID first, then count status rows.
Output: start the reply with TICKET CHECK, show the count of unique tickets, and validate that the status counts reconcile to the unique total. Duplicate rows are not counted as tickets.

SHARED RULE
In both cases derive the total arithmetically from its components - supplied counts in Case 1, deduplicated counts in Case 2. Never output a total that contradicts its parts. If the parts cannot be made to reconcile, say so plainly rather than adjusting numbers.

UNDEFINED CASES - ASK, DO NOT GUESS
Leave these open for clarification instead of inventing a rule or silently picking a case:
- only one of the two counts is supplied;
- a ticket ID carries conflicting statuses;
- status values fall outside the categories present in the log;
- the input is neither supplied counts nor a ticket log.
